title: Meralco electricity rates rise in October 2026 as generation costs rise
summary: Expect too Meralco's higher distribution charges to kick in next month, but a newly approved refund could soften that impact on consumers

items: Meralco customers will see a 32-centavo increase per kilowatt-hour in electricity bills this October, raising the overall residential rate to P15.0615.

The increase is primarily due to higher generation costs linked to elevated fuel prices and tighter electricity supply, although some costs were offset by cheaper electricity from other suppliers and reduced taxes.
Starting in November, Meralco will implement a higher distribution charge approved by the Energy Regulatory Commission, but this will be partially mitigated by a P2.64-billion refund to customers.

MANILA, Philippines – Meralco customers will face higher electricity bills this October, as the energy giant announced a 32-centavo hike per kilowatt-hour (kWh).
The Manila Electric Company (Meralco) said on Tuesday, October 13, that its overall residential electricity rate will rise by P0.3191 per kWh, bringing it to P15.0615 from P14.7424 in September.
For a household consuming 200 kWh monthly, this translates to an additional P64 on the electricity bill, bringing the total to around P3,012.

blocks.caption: Meralco electricity rates rise in October 2026 as generation costs rise

blocks.text: Most of the increase was because of higher generation costs, which rose by P0.4973 per kWh amid elevated fuel prices, a weaker peso, and tighter electricity supply.

Meralco said electricity purchased from First Gas and Prime CoreGen became more expensive as the plants used liquefied natural gas (LNG), whose price remains elevated due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

blocks.caption: DRIVERS. Screenshot showing the drivers of electricity rates, taken from Meralco’s press conference on Tuesday.

blocks.text: Meanwhile, electricity purchased from the Wholesale Electricity Spot Market (WESM) also became more expensive due to tighter supply conditions in Luzon.
These increases were only partly offset by cheaper electricity from other contracted suppliers, lower transmission charges, and reduced taxes.
The removal of the 12% value-added tax on allowable system loss charges also helped reduce the overall increase.

blocks.caption: With power bills already high, Meralco wins approval to raise own fees after 15 years

blocks.text: The October rate does not yet include the newly approved increase in Meralco’s own distribution charges, which the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) approved following the distribution utility’s first rate review in 15 years.
Unlike generation and transmission charges, which are pass-through fees, distribution charges pay for Meralco’s own operations and allow it to earn a regulated profit.
The ERC approved an average distribution rate of P1.48 per kWh, up from the existing P1.35, although Meralco has yet to determine the exact impact on residential customers.

Meralco spokesperson Joe Zaldarriaga said the company expects to implement the higher distribution rate beginning November billing, which will be slightly offset by a newly approved P2.64-billion refund to customers.

The refund, equivalent to P0.1733 per kWh for residential customers, will run for six months or until the full amount is returned. It could offset much of the impact of the distribution rate increase, with Zaldarriaga saying the two adjustments could result in a slight net reduction in charges.
Meralco is also continuing two previously approved refunds totaling P1.0139 per kWh for residential customers.

Asked by Rappler whether Meralco’s planned investments to reduce system losses were considered in the rate reset, Meralco head of utility economics Larry Fernandez confirmed that the company had included spending proposals to bring down these losses. (READ: MAP: Where have system losses been highest from 2021 to 2025?)

However, Fernandez said Meralco could not yet identify which projects regulators had approved, reduced, or rejected. As such, the company also did not provide specific targets or timelines for reducing technical and non-technical system losses. – Rappler.com
